messages:
maria: Quick question — should the gateway expose an "early_quiesce" signal to the edge proxy when we start sending a response body but want to stop accepting additional request-side processing? Trying to reconcile retry behavior with partial streaming and billing.
alex: Do you mean like an explicit 'we've started sending payload, but please quiesce any stateful retries and flush what you have' flag?
ravi: Yeah, similar. We ran into this with the long-polling clients: gateway forwarded a partial chunk then upstream retried and duplicated side effects.
jen: TL;DR: we need an interface distinction between safe idempotent retries vs abort-and-replay. An "early_quiesce" would let the edge know to stop hedging but keep delivering in-flight stream.
maria: Exactly. Implementation idea: gateway attaches a header on the forwarded request: `x-rwq-early-quiesce: 1` once it begins streaming body to client. The edge treats that as a downgrade of retry budget for side-effecting routes.
alex: Concern: what if the gateway later reconnects (client reconnects) and expects resume? How do we preserve progress without allowing upstream to re-run side effects?
ravi: Two pieces: 1) a resumable KV checkpoint token in trailers (opaque to gateway), 2) a retry policy change when `x-rwq-early-quiesce` present. Edge should persist checkpoint tokens and disallow non-idempotent retries unless client explicitly issues a replay with idempotency-key.
jen: We should standardize the trailer shape. Something like:
```
Trailer: x-rwq-checkpoint: token_v1:<base64>
Trailer: x-rwq-sideeffect-safe: true|false
```
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary gateway v2.3.1 to staging queued (owners: @alex). :construction:
bob: (not in thread) -- ignoring
maria: Also need to decide billing: if gateway starts streaming and then cancels mid-stream due to client timeout, do we bill tokens up to last confirmed trailer or up to last byte sent? Product wants a deterministic rule.
alex: Our current rule is billed up to server-side completion event. For streaming, that maps to final chunk + trailers. Suggest: bill up to last acknowledged trailer or last committed checkpoint. If no trailer, bill up to last CHUNK_RECEIVED event timestamp.
ravi: Edge runtime change: when it sees `x-rwq-early-quiesce`, it should reduce hedge windows to 0 and disable speculative retries. Also persist `x-rwq-checkpoint` when present. Add metrics: `edge.quiesce.disabled_retries` and `edge.quiesce.resume_tokens_persisted`.
jen: API contract draft for gateway<->edge:
- Header `x-rwq-early-quiesce: 1` sent once gateway begins client stream
- Edge must treat affected requests as "no speculative retries" and record a `quiesce` tag in trace
- Trailer `x-rwq-checkpoint` may be emitted at stream end; gateway must persist and surface to client if requested
- If stream ends without trailer, gateway may mark request as "partial_stream" and expose a resume path only if client provided idempotency key
maria: Sounds good. Any concerns about backward compatibility?
alex: For older edges, header is ignored -> behavior stays as-is (which may allow speculative retries). We should gate rollout: gateway sends header only to edge instances >= runtime v1.7 with feature flag `quiesce-handshake`.
ravi: Ops note: need migration doc for Dedicated customers, since they might have custom routers. Also add a debug dump endpoint to list currently persisted resume tokens (admin only).
jen: I'll sketch an RFC with the header/trailer shapes, metrics and rollout plan. Can we get a quick +1 from @alex and @ravi before EOD so I can post it to the architecture board?
alex: +1
ravi: +1
maria: Thanks — will loop back with the RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
